promotions.claim: Teardown decides whether a `.env*` file is work or scratch by byte-comparing it against the main checkout. The decision is 'is this deletable', the proxy is 'is it identical to main' — so a worktree that correctly carries its own port is byte-different and blocks teardown on every correct setup. `CONTEXT.md` bakes the same comparison into the glossary definition of Scratch, so the proxy is not a local implementation detail.

promotion.spread: none — identical output on every repetition
promotion.observed: arm `identical` -> no block; arm `per-port` (PORT=3101) -> block `.env — differs from the main checkout copy`
promotion.scope: the shipped classifier at src/scripts tree of the census commit; both arms are throwaway git repositories under a temp root

evidence: scripts/worktree-lifecycle/classify.py:253-262 — `_env_problem` returns 'differs from the main checkout copy'
CONTEXT.md:206-213 — the Scratch definition carries the same comparison

promotions.claim: `targets_linked_worktree` authorizes a risky command when the command *string contains* a linked-worktree path. A command that merely mentions such a path — in a comment or an unrelated echo — is authorized while operating elsewhere; the same predicate cannot be satisfied at all by a command that legitimately operates outside the repository, which is then blocked. The mandate carried this as a hypothesis; the fixture demonstrates both directions.

promotion.spread: none — identical output on every repetition
promotion.observed: `git push --force origin main` -> block; the same command with `# see .worktrees/380-truth-census` appended -> allow; `echo "/fixture/repo/.worktrees/380-truth-census" && git push --force origin main` -> allow; `cd /srv/other-checkout && git push --force origin main` -> block
promotion.scope: synthetic RepoFacts; no repository is read and no command is executed

promotions.claim: The risky-command gate itself is a naive regex: the default pattern `\bgit\s+(?:commit|push)\b` does not match `git -C <path> push`, so the most direct way to push from the protected main checkout while pointing at another repository is not classified risky at all and never reaches the authorization branch. This is a fail-open one step upstream of the substring defect, found by the same fixture.

promotion.observed: `git -C /srv/other-checkout push --force origin main` -> allow, targetsLinkedWorktree=false, i.e. never classified risky

promotions.claim: The `## Prod` readiness section is located by exact string equality (`line.trim() === '## Prod'`). A consumer heading that carries its own wording — `## Prod und Deployment`, `## Prod:` — reports `missing-section`, the same code an entirely absent section reports. Two different states collapse onto one, and the collapse is where the false 'you have not configured this' is born. testreporter#2283 is that failure in a live consumer.

promotion.observed: `## Prod` -> valid; `## Prod und Deployment` -> missing-section; `## Prod:` -> missing-section; `## Deployment` (genuinely absent) -> missing-section
promotion.scope: the shipped `inspectProdSections` against throwaway CLAUDE.md files in a temp directory

promotions.claim: `README.md:407` promises that a file the consumer did not touch fast-forwards to the new version. The reconcile is all-or-nothing: `update` returns `conflicted` and activates nothing as soon as ANY file conflicts, so in the very situation the sentence is written for — the consumer edited something — no untouched file fast-forwards. The counter-control's no-conflict arm is green, which isolates the claim to the conflict path rather than to the reconcile as a whole.

promotion.observed: shipped arm C1 fail (untouched file keeps v1 bytes, update state `conflicted`); shippedNoConflict arm C1 pass
promotion.scope: src/ tree 7143160ed66ae6efd562ec1b3966ceb09d6a2c39, consumer fixture built in a temp directory

promotions.claim: The `**Retro:**` line is bound as hard as the kit binds anything — a machine-checked closed value set, a blocking question, and a second `$wrapup` invocation — and its yield over the whole merged history is 10. Recounted from the frozen export at the substrate freeze: 135 merged pull requests, 74 carrying the marker, 14 carrying any findings heading, 10 of the marker-carrying PRs carrying one, 2 carrying a Meta section. The sensor is the only instrument that reports whether planning was good, so it is kept; the binding is the finding.
